title: Inﬂuence of the Accuracy of Topographic Data in the Estimation of Flood Flows: A Case Study of L’Horteta Ravine (Spain)
content: Many critical characteristics of exceptional events such as flooding caused by extreme rainfall remain unknown, yet they are essential for advancing geoscientific analyses of their impacts. In this paper, flooding caused by storm DANA on October 29, 2024, in the Spanish region of Valencia is studied. Particularly the hydraulic modeling of the DANA event in the L'Horteta ravine is conducted. Deriving an accurate estimate of the discharge values constituted the primary objective of the study, as substantial uncertainty still surrounds the magnitude of the flows generated during this catastrophic event. To address it, commonly used approximate digital elevation models are compared against purpose‑built, high‑precision geometric ones. Actual flood traces collected on field are used to calibrate and validate hydraulic simulations. Results show purpose‑built, high‑precision models provide a reliable simulation. An estimated peak discharge of 4,129 m³/s was found, exceeding both the official records and the 500-year return period typical values. In contrast, approximate digital elevation models tend to underestimate peak discharge and produce substantially larger flood areas. This discrepancy highlights the critical importance of ensuring both consistency and precision of cartographic data to guarantee the reliability of hydraulic simulations and improve flood risk assessment and management.
